newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters resume talks to avert strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters resume talks to avert strike.

text.p: The International Brotherhood of Teamsters and United Parcel Service, the biggest U.S. parcel carrier, resumed contract talks on Sunday evening in a last-ditch bid to avert a threatened strike.

Teamsters president Ron Carey repeated the union's threat to walk out at a midnight EDT deadline, if no new contract had been agreed. "If the company does not address the issues ... I assure you at 12:01, we'll be on strike," Carey told reporters as the union delegation arrived for the talks.

"We are willing and ready to continue talking with the Teamsters this evening," said UPS spokeswoman Gina Ellrich, noting that the threat of a strike had already reduced the carrier's shipping volume by one million packages from 12 million, forcing it to lay off several thousand workers.
"We are working hard to resolve the issues together," she said.

Carey said the union had submitted a comprehensive contract proposal to the federal mediator Saturday evening, but the company had not yet responded. He said the union was particularly concerned about preventing work going to subcontractors rather than union workers, the pension plan and health and safety issues.
UPS Chairman and CEO James Kelly and his negotiating team arrived around 6:30 p.m. EDT to meet with the mediator and consider the union proposal.
